criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: API_KEYS was set as an encrypted Vercel env var by piping BENCH_API_KEYS through node into the API without printing it, and the app reads it from process.env. No secrets appear in the source or the deployed files. The only small issue is that the Vercel token was passed on the command line (`--token $VERCEL_TOKEN`).

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: Production was deployed with the Vercel CLI straight from the agent's working directory, and the remote build ran on that uploaded source with a lockfile present. Some build inputs float: the CLI was `npx -y vercel@latest`, dependencies use caret ranges, and `engines.node` is `>=20`.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a personal project, so the non-commercial Hobby plan fits, and Hobby functions don't expire or sleep. However, the app relies on persistent storage that was never provisioned: the Neon terms were not accepted and Blob creation hit the Hobby usage threshold. The live service therefore doesn't meet its data requirement.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The deployment is a single serverless function with no extra public resources and no data store to expose. API_KEYS is also scoped to Preview deployments, so preview URLs accept the production keys too.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: The app is served over HTTPS with a valid certificate. Plain HTTP gets a 308 redirect to HTTPS, and the platform adds HSTS with preload. The app sets no X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, although Express or vercel.json `headers` could have added them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Without a public/ directory and with an all-paths rewrite in vercel.json, Vercel serves uploaded files that exist on disk as static assets. As a result /lib/app.js, /lib/db.js, /lib/store.js, /lib/openapi.js, /scripts/dev.js and /TASK.md are all publicly downloadable. They contain no secrets. Probes for .env, .git, .vercel and package.json returned the app's JSON 404, and errors don't leak stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input validation, parameterized SQL, hashed key ownership with 404 for other keys, and generic 500s are all done well. But the live store is the in-memory fallback, so notes are lost when an instance recycles. The 60/min rate limit is kept per instance, so concurrent instances multiply it, and stored data is unbounded in memory.

findings.title: Application source files served publicly as static assets
findings.evidence: GET https://adb-lfmyb-api.vercel.app/lib/app.js -> 200 application/javascript (full source, content-disposition: inline; filename="app.js"). /lib/db.js, /lib/store.js, /lib/openapi.js, /scripts/dev.js and /TASK.md also return 200. vercel.json only has a rewrite `/(.*)` -> `/api`, and rewrites don't apply to paths that exist on the filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Move the server code under api/ (or a directory Vercel doesn't serve), list lib/, scripts/ and TASK.md in .vercelignore, keep them only as function includes, or declare an explicit outputDirectory/public folder so only intended assets are served.

findings.title: Live service runs on a non-persistent, per-instance in-memory store
findings.evidence: lib/store.js getStore(): with no DATABASE_URL it falls back to memoryStore(). process/deployment.json: 'Persistent storage is NOT in place yet ... data lives in memory per function instance'. deploy.md: every `integration add` returned integration_terms_acceptance_required, and Blob creation returned usage_threshold_limits_reached.
findings.recommendation: Provision Postgres (accept the Neon terms and attach DATABASE_URL), and make the app fail closed instead of silently serving a volatile store in production.

findings.title: Rate limit not enforced globally without the database
findings.evidence: lib/store.js memoryStore().hitRateLimit keeps counters in a per-instance Map. When Vercel scales out, each instance allows 60 requests per minute per key.
findings.recommendation: Back the rate limiter with shared storage (the Postgres rate_limits table or a KV/Redis store).

findings.title: No size limits on note fields or count; memory can grow unbounded
findings.evidence: lib/app.js validateFields checks only types, plus the express.json 1mb limit. memoryStore holds every note in a Map with no cap.
findings.recommendation: Cap the title, content and tag lengths, the number of tags, and the notes per key.

findings.title: Required persistent storage not provisioned on the chosen plan
findings.evidence: deploy.md: Neon/Prisma/Supabase/AWS integrations need terms acceptance in a browser, and POST /v1/storage/stores/blob -> usage_threshold_limits_reached on the hobby team. TASK.md requires storage that survives restarts and redeploys.
findings.recommendation: Complete the human step to attach a free Neon database, or use another storage option available to the account.

findings.title: Missing security headers the app could set
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-lfmyb-api.vercel.app/health: only strict-transport-security (added by the platform). No x-content-type-options, x-frame-options/frame-ancestors or content-security-policy.
findings.recommendation: Add the headers in Express middleware (e.g. helmet) or in vercel.json `headers`.

findings.title: Unpinned deploy tooling and runtime
findings.evidence: deploy.md: every command uses `npx -y vercel@latest`. package.json has "express": "^5.3.0", "pg": "^8.23.1", and "engines": {"node": ">=20"} (the build warned it will auto-upgrade).
findings.recommendation: Pin the Vercel CLI version and the Node major (e.g. "20.x"), and rely on the committed package-lock.json with npm ci.

findings.title: Production API keys also valid on preview deployments
findings.evidence: deploy.md: env POST with target ["production","preview"] for API_KEYS.
findings.recommendation: Scope production keys to production only, and use separate keys for previews if they're needed.

findings.title: Vercel token passed as a CLI argument
findings.evidence: deploy.md: `npx -y vercel@latest --token $VERCEL_TOKEN ...`. The value is redacted in logs, but it's visible in the process list on the build host.
findings.recommendation: Pass it via the VERCEL_TOKEN environment variable instead of --token.

findings.title: HTTPS enforced with HSTS by platform
findings.evidence: curl -sI http://adb-lfmyb-api.vercel.app/health -> 308 Location: https://...; HTTPS responses carry strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload.

security.summary: The Notes API on Vercel Hobby fits this personal use. Secrets are handled well: API_KEYS is an encrypted env var and nothing leaks into logs or files, and HTTPS with HSTS is enforced. The main weaknesses: the server source (/lib/*.js, /scripts/dev.js, TASK.md) is publicly downloadable as static files, and there is no database, so notes live in a volatile per-instance memory store and the per-key rate limit only holds within each instance. Smaller issues are unpinned tooling (vercel@latest, node >=20), missing app-level security headers and preview-scoped production keys.

busy.basis: exceeds Hobby's limits (CDN requests, function invocations, active CPU), which pauses the project, so priced on Pro: $20 platform fee including $20 of usage credit, $5.75 of usage

final_messages.build:
The Notes API is built and every requirement in `TASK.md` works locally. The 4 automated tests pass, and I also checked it by hand with curl, including a restart to confirm notes are kept.

**Stack**
- **Node.js with Express 5**, running on Vercel as a single serverless function. `api/index.js` exports the app, and `vercel.json` sends every path to it.
- **PostgreSQL** through the `pg` driver. It reads `DATABASE_URL`, or `POSTGRES_URL` as a fallback, which is the variable a Vercel-provided Neon database sets. The tables are created automatically on the first request.
- **Rate limit** (60 requests per minute per key) is also stored in Postgres, so it still holds when Vercel runs several copies of the function at once. Each key's minute starts at its first request, and a request over the limit gets `429` with `Retry-After`.
- **API keys** come from `API_KEYS`. They are stored only as hashes and each note is tied to the key that created it, so other keys get `404`.
- **Docs:** `/openapi.json` serves the OpenAPI 3 document, and `/docs` serves an HTML page built from it with no external dependencies.

**Code layout:** the routes, auth and validation are in `lib/app.js`, the database code in `lib/db.js`, the OpenAPI document and docs page in `lib/openapi.js`, and the tests in `test/api.test.js`.

**Run locally**
```sh
docker run -d --name notes-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
npm install
API_KEYS=key-one,key-two DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres npm start   # http://localhost:3000
npm test   # needs that Postgres running, or DATABASE_URL set
```

**What step 2 needs:** a Postgres database attached to the Vercel project (for example Neon from the Vercel Marketplace) and the `API_KEYS` environment variable set. There is no build step.

I stopped the local server and removed the Postgres container.
final_messages.deploy:
The API is live at **https://adb-lfmyb-api.vercel.app**, and every endpoint passed my tests through that URL. One requirement is not met: notes are not stored persistently yet. Every database option on Vercel needs a person to act first.

**What's deployed:** one Vercel project, `adb-lfmyb-api`, on the free Hobby plan, so the cost is $0 a month. `API_KEYS` is set to exactly the keys in `BENCH_API_KEYS`, stored encrypted.

**What I checked through the public URL:**
- `/health`, `/openapi.json` and `/docs` all return `200`.
- A missing or unknown key gets `401`.
- Creating a note without a title gets `400`.
- Create, list with the `tag` filter, update and delete all work.
- A second key gets `404` on the first key's note and sees an empty list.
- After 60 requests in a minute, the key gets `429` with a `Retry-After` header, while the other key is unaffected.

**What didn't work: no database.**
- **Marketplace databases:** Neon, Prisma Postgres, Supabase and AWS all need their terms accepted in a browser first.
- **Vercel Blob:** creating a store failed because the team has hit a usage limit (`usage_threshold_limits_reached`).

So I added a fallback that keeps everything in memory whenever no database address (`DATABASE_URL`) is set. As a result, notes and rate-limit counts are lost when Vercel restarts or redeploys the app. If Vercel runs more than one copy at once, each copy also has its own separate data. The Postgres version is unchanged and passes the tests against a local Postgres, as does the fallback.

**The one step a person needs to do** (also listed under `human_steps` in `deployment.json`):
1. Accept the Neon terms at https://vercel.com/ai-deploy-bench/~/integrations/accept-terms/neon?source=cli
2. In this directory, run `vercel integration add neon --name adb-lfmyb-api-db`, then `vercel deploy --prod`.

After that the app switches to Postgres on its own and creates its tables; no code changes are needed.

I didn't create any credentials, so there was nothing to save in `.env`. I added a `.vercelignore` so env files and tests are never uploaded.

human_steps.step: Open https://vercel.com/ai-deploy-bench/~/integrations/accept-terms/neon?source=cli and accept the Neon marketplace terms for the ai-deploy-bench team. Then run (in this directory): `vercel --scope team_U2tHOV4fpUx18nl9EpcRQ4hO integration add neon --name adb-lfmyb-api-db` (free plan) and `vercel deploy --prod`.
human_steps.why: Provisions the Postgres database (Neon free tier, connected to the project as DATABASE_URL). Without it the app runs on its in-memory fallback, so notes and rate-limit counters do not survive restarts/redeploys and are not shared across function instances. No code changes are needed: when DATABASE_URL is present the app uses Postgres and creates its tables automatically.

deployment_manifest.notes: All endpoints, auth (API_KEYS = BENCH_API_KEYS, set as an encrypted env var for production and preview), per-key ownership (404 for other keys), validation and per-key rate limiting (60/min, 429 + Retry-After) were verified through the public URL. Persistent storage is NOT in place yet: every Vercel Marketplace database (Neon, Prisma Postgres, Supabase, AWS) requires terms acceptance in a browser, and creating a first-party Vercel Blob store failed with 'usage_threshold_limits_reached' on this hobby team. Until the human step is done, data lives in memory per function instance and is lost when the instance is recycled or redeployed. The Postgres backend is implemented and tested locally against Postgres 16.
